core_obligations: Write the target as the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible ring, fix a fundamental system of weak ideals of definition, and observe that each base change of the source is affine with surjective structure map (proof lines 6146-6155).
Conclude that the structure maps of the limit are surjective, hence that the source is a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 6155-6160).
Establish tautness of the corresponding ring map from representability and affineness of the immersion (proof lines 6160-6163).
Show that the kernel is closed, using completeness of the target and continuity of the map, and that the image is dense, using surjectivity of the maps to the quotients (proof lines 6163-6166).
proof_roadmap: Base changes and surjectivity of the quotient maps (proof lines 6146-6155).
Tautness, closed kernel and dense image (proof lines 6160-6166).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the source of a closed immersion of formal algebraic spaces into a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space is again McQuillan affine, and that the immersion corresponds to a continuous homomorphism of weakly admissible algebras which is taut, has closed kernel and dense image (statement lines 6137-6144). The proof writes the target as the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible ring, fixes a fundamental system of weak ideals of definition, and observes that each base change of the source is a closed subscheme of an affine scheme, hence affine, and that the corresponding ring maps are surjective (proof lines 6146-6155). The surjectivity of the structure maps of the limit then makes the source McQuillan, by the criterion for that type (proof lines 6155-6160). Tautness of the ring map is read off from representability and affineness of the immersion, the kernel is closed because the target ring is complete and the map is continuous, and density of the image follows from the surjectivity of the maps to the quotients (proof lines 6160-6166). The claim is H2: the argument produces the presentation of the source and then verifies four separate properties of the induced ring map, each with its own reason.
